value.rationale: A motivated current gap is the reversible-only all-time Frobenius guarantee for Gibbs-averaged chains. This theorem extends it to an important nonreversible class even when averaging destroys normality, controls arbitrary baselines by a computable time-two commutator penalty, and establishes a universally sharp quantitative finite-time improvement term. It informs partition selection and robustness to nonnormality rather than simply recomputing a known table. Computational transition costs and unknown wider literature are acknowledged.
